headline: Run frontier AI entirely on your machine with llama.cpp, no API keys or telemetry
summary: llama.cpp allows you to own your models and conversation data, offering a local, private, and limitless way to deploy advanced AI models without external dependencies.
details: llama.cpp enables users to run frontier AI models directly on their own machines, eliminating the need for API keys, telemetry, or external limits. This gives users full ownership of their models and conversation data, ensuring privacy and control.

Setup is streamlined: simply run `llama serve`, install the `pi-llama` plugin, and launch Pi. The system automatically discovers your local model, requiring no configuration or API keys, with all files and requests remaining on your machine.

The platform is highly versatile, running on hardware ranging from laptops to clusters with the same binary, models, and hand-tuned kernels for various GPUs and CPUs. This ensures consistent performance across diverse environments.

llama.cpp supports a wide array of advanced open models, including Alibaba's next-gen natively multimodal reasoning models, Google's Gemini 3-based open models for multimodal reasoning and agentic workflows, and OpenAI's first open-weight models since GPT-2, designed for reasoning and developer use with function calling.

headline_marked: [[Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones show up]] in FCC filing ahead of September launch
headline: Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones show up in FCC filing ahead of September launch
summary: The rumored over-ear headphones, potentially named 'Ace Ultra', are expected to launch in September and come in five new colors, expanding on the original Ace design.
details: Sonos' upcoming 'Ace Ultra' over-ear headphones have appeared in an FCC filing, hinting at a September product launch. The filing, spotted by Lowpass, suggests an over-ear design similar to the original Sonos Ace, but with five new color options: Greige, Shadow Black, Agave, Blush, and Sand.

The FCC documents also indicate support for Sonos Voice Control, the company's proprietary voice assistant. This feature is crucial for screenless devices to interact with AI, aligning with CEO Thomas Conrad's strategy to integrate AI deeply into Sonos' business.

This new model follows the original Sonos Ace launch, which faced issues with a faulty app upgrade and a delayed TrueCinema spatial audio enhancement feature. TrueCinema, designed to adapt spatial audio based on a room's acoustics and Sonos soundbars, was released a year after the initial headphones.

The Ace Ultra is likely part of a broader push into AI-enabled products by Sonos. Conrad believes the company has a unique advantage in home AI, leveraging its ecosystem of interconnected audio devices.
